answer: Deposit plus arbitration forfeiture resists sybils. Before it can vote or grade, every identity must escrow a fixed deposit and ink its receipt with its own quill, a unique signing instrument bound permanently to that key. The amount sits at the summit of the collateral schedule: one full deposit per identity, so a farm minting 1000 clones pays 1000× that deposit, each frozen in glacier escrow until a rotating arbitration panel rules. Proven duplicates forfeit their entire deposit to the challenger, so honesty stays cheaper.
